method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA) 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy' (content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition)), 13 claims; LICENCE: © ASCIA 2026; no reuse terms stated (read at the page footer ('© ASCIA 2026, Content updated June 2026')). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA' (published April 2024), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (© 2024 The Author(s)) (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11068951). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the WAO DRACMA 2024 GRADE recommendations on which formula to use and in what order, because ASCIA's formula-by-type table (S1) could not be machine-read. S1's claims and anchors are unchanged. S2 is CC BY-NC-ND and is paraphrased and hash-anchored; its qualifying remarks are kept with each recommendation as WAO asks. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S2 Table 1 (the Recommendation 3 and 4 remarks on probiotic formulas) and Table 2 (what a conditional recommendation means).

claims.claim: **Breastfeeding comes first** because of its benefits for mother and baby; this guidance is for when it is not possible.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A breastfeeding mother does not necessarily need to cut out cow's milk.** Discuss it with a medical specialist, and have a dietitian supervise any exclusion.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eczema on its own does not justify a specialised infant formula.**
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🚩 **Do not use these for CMA:** partially hydrolysed or A2 formula, any standard formula (anti-reflux, lactose-free, organic, newborn or follow-on types included), or goat and other animal milks. Unlisted plant or vegan formulas lack hypoallergenicity and growth data.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rice-protein formula is an option unless the child is allergic to rice,** but evidence for it in non-IgE food allergy is limited. Of the two in Australia, only Novalac Allergy has product-specific hypoallergenicity and growth studies; Alula Allergy is batch-tested for milk and soy contamination.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use amino acid formula (AAF) or extensively hydrolysed formula (eHF) when growth is poor or there are several non-IgE food allergies.**
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **IgE-mediated CMA, infant not breastfed: first choice is an extensively hydrolysed cow's milk formula (eHF) or a hydrolysed rice formula; second, amino acid formula (AAF); third, soy formula.** Conditional recommendation, very low certainty evidence.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🚩 **Never give a formula the child has already reacted to,** and warn that a few children react the first time they take eHF or soy formula (whether this happens with rice formula is unknown).
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Non-IgE-mediated CMA, infant not breastfed: the same order** (eHF or hydrolysed rice formula, then AAF, then soy; conditional, very low certainty). Where soy is an option, think about soy sensitisation in a child who has not settled on eHF, such as one with FPIES or FPIAP.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Eosinophilic oesophagitis: evidence exists only for AAF,** so the panel advises avoiding eHF, rice and soy formulas for now, with rice formula second if AAF cannot be had. **FPIES to milk or rice, or rice tolerance unknown:** do not use hydrolysed rice formula.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Why the order is only a suggestion:** in very low certainty evidence, eHF may favour outgrowing CMA compared with AAF (RR 2.32) but may support weight and length gain less well than AAF. The choice should be made individually with the carer, weighing the child's severity, tolerance and taste of the formula, local availability and what is funded.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Cost matters for equity:** AAF is usually the dearest, eHF and rice formula cost less but are still expensive in many places, and soy is usually the cheapest.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Probiotic-containing formula (IgE or non-IgE CMA): either a formula without a probiotic, or a casein-based eHF with *Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus* GG (LGG),** is suggested (conditional, very low certainty); LGG-casein eHF is the only combination studied. Children with immune deficiency may be at more risk from probiotics, though this has not been studied.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **S2's summary table adds, for non-IgE CMA, a second studied combination:** casein eHF with *L. casei* CRL431 and *B. lactis* Bb12, though no such formula is on the market. Neither probiotic recommendation covers infants whose CMA has not been confirmed.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **What 'conditional' means here:** most families would choose the suggested option but many would not, so the clinician accepts that different choices suit different infants and helps each family reach a decision matching its own values and preferences; decision aids can help.
claims.locator: World Allergy Organization (Bognanni A, Fiocchi A, Arasi S, et al.), World Allergy Organization Journal 17(4):100888, doi 10.1016/j.waojou.2024.100888, 'World Allergy Organization (WAO) Diagnosis and Rationale for Action against Cow's Milk Allergy (DRACMA) guideline update - XII - Recommendations on milk formula supplements with and without probiotics for infants and toddlers with CMA', published April 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11068951/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If the usual formula is unavailable, swap within the same group** (one eHF for another eHF), after reviewing why it was first chosen and any change in history.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A thriving child over 6 months** whose earlier reaction to cow's milk formula was mild or moderate, and who was put on eHF before 6 months, can be switched to soy formula.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If AAF for over-12-month-olds is needed but unavailable, involve a paediatric allergy dietitian** to adapt a substitute recipe. With any formula change, go over the mixing instructions with the family, since scoop-to-water ratios differ a lot.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Over 12 months on soy formula:** calcium-fortified soy milk can take its place, provided growth is good and the child eats a broad range of family foods.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allergic to both cow's milk and soy:** most plant milks without calcium fortification (such as rice or soy milk) have too little protein, fat and calcium for young children unless growth and nutrition are carefully checked.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Up to four years of age, 400-500 mL a day of calcium-fortified plant milk meets calcium needs;** drinking more can blunt appetite, intake and growth.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every infant or child with CMA should see a paediatric allergy dietitian** for a nutrition assessment.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23
